i need a back-end for a podcast website. right now i need to define the API for the people who are creating the front-end so we can work concurrently.   Prioritize browsing titles and serving the media. it is important that the media is played serverside, not downloaded to client. python with html5 and flask hosted on localhost.

Outline & Summary

Since this could get detailed, here's a quick outline:

  1. Assumptions & Setup: Basic Flask app with SQLite for storing podcast data (titles, files). Media files assumed in a local directory.
  2. API Endpoints: Focus on browsing titles and streaming media (server-side, no direct download).
  3. Streaming Implementation: Use Flask's streaming response with range support for HTML5 audio playback.
  4. Sample Code: Full Flask app code to get you started.
  5. Next Steps: How to run/test, and what to expand.

If you want to dive deeper into any part (e.g., auth, more endpoints), or if I missed inputs (like sample data schema), let me know. Otherwise, here's the full response.

Assumptions

  • Podcasts have episodes with: id, title, description, file_path (e.g., to MP3 files in a ./media/ folder).
  • Simple SQLite DB for metadata (no full podcast RSS parsing yet).
  • Front-end will use HTML5 <audio> tags pointing to your stream endpoint (e.g., <audio src="/stream/1" controls></audio>).
  • No auth/security yet (add later if needed).
  • Media streaming: We'll use send_file with partial content (HTTP 206) to stream, preventing easy full downloads.
  • Hosted on localhost:5000.

Required Dependencies

Install via pip:

  • Flask
  • flask-sqlalchemy (for DB)
Bash
pip install flask flask-sqlalchemy

Database Setup

We'll use SQLite to store episode info. Create a models.py or inline in app.

Example schema:

  • Episode: id (int), title (str), description (str), file_path (str)

Flask App Structure

Create a file like app.py. Here's the full code:

Python
from flask import Flask, jsonify, request, send_file, abort
from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy
import os

app = Flask(__name__)
app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///podcasts.db'
app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False
app.config['MEDIA_FOLDER'] = './media'  # Folder for your MP3 files

db = SQLAlchemy(app)

# Database Model
class Episode(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(200), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=True)
    file_path = db.Column(db.String(200), nullable=False)  # e.g., 'episode1.mp3'

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            'id': self.id,
            'title': self.title,
            'description': self.description
        }

# Create DB if not exists (run once)
with app.app_context():
    db.create_all()

# API Endpoints

# 1. List all episodes (browsing titles)
@app.route('/episodes', methods=['GET'])
def get_episodes():
    """
    Get list of episodes.
    Query params: ?page=1&limit=10 (optional, default all)
    Response: JSON array of {id, title, description}
    """
    page = request.args.get('page', 1, type=int)
    limit = request.args.get('limit', 10, type=int)
    episodes = Episode.query.paginate(page=page, per_page=limit, error_out=False)
    return jsonify({
        'episodes': [ep.to_dict() for ep in episodes.items],
        'total': episodes.total,
        'pages': episodes.pages,
        'current_page': episodes.page
    })

# 2. Get single episode details
@app.route('/episode/<int:episode_id>', methods=['GET'])
def get_episode(episode_id):
    """
    Get details for one episode.
    Response: JSON {id, title, description}
    """
    episode = Episode.query.get_or_404(episode_id)
    return jsonify(episode.to_dict())

# 3. Stream media (server-side playback)
@app.route('/stream/<int:episode_id>', methods=['GET'])
def stream_episode(episode_id):
    """
    Stream audio file for episode.
    Supports range requests for seeking in HTML5 audio.
    Headers: Accept-Ranges: bytes, Content-Type: audio/mpeg
    No direct download; front-end uses <audio src="/stream/{id}"> to play.
    """
    episode = Episode.query.get_or_404(episode_id)
    file_path = os.path.join(app.config['MEDIA_FOLDER'], episode.file_path)
    
    if not os.path.exists(file_path):
        abort(404, description="Media file not found")
    
    range_header = request.headers.get('Range', None)
    return send_file(
        file_path,
        mimetype='audio/mpeg',
        conditional=True,  # Handles range requests
        as_attachment=False  # Streams instead of downloading
    )

# Bonus: Add new episode (for admin/testing)
@app.route('/episode', methods=['POST'])
def add_episode():
    """
    Add episode (JSON body: {title, description, file_path})
    Response: JSON of new episode
    """
    data = request.json
    if not data or not data.get('title') or not data.get('file_path'):
        abort(400, description="Missing title or file_path")
    
    episode = Episode(
        title=data['title'],
        description=data.get('description'),
        file_path=data['file_path']
    )
    db.session.add(episode)
    db.session.commit()
    return jsonify(episode.to_dict()), 201

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(debug=True, host='localhost', port=5000)

API Documentation

Share this with your front-end team:

  • Base URL: http://localhost:5000
  1. Browse Episodes
    • Method: GET /episodes?page=1&limit=10
    • Response: 200 OK, JSON
      JSON
      {
  "episodes": [
    {"id": 1, "title": "Episode 1", "description": "Intro"},
    ...
  ],
  "total": 5,
  "pages": 1,
  "current_page": 1
}
    • Errors: 500 if DB issue.
  2. Get Episode Details
    • Method: GET /episode/{id} (e.g., /episode/1)
    • Response: 200 OK, JSON {id: 1, title: "...", description: "..."}
    • Errors: 404 if not found.
  3. Stream Media
    • Method: GET /stream/{id} (e.g., /stream/1)
    • Response: 200/206 OK, audio/mpeg stream (partial if Range header sent). Headers:
      • Content-Type: audio/mpeg
      • Accept-Ranges: bytes
      • Content-Range: bytes start-end/total (for seeking)
    • Front-end usage: <audio src="http://localhost:5000/stream/1" controls></audio> – plays server-side, supports pause/seek without full download.
    • Errors: 404 if episode/file missing, 416 if invalid range.
  • Add Episode (optional for now): POST /episode with JSON body.

How to Run & Test

  1. Create ./media/ folder, add sample MP3s (e.g., episode1.mp3).
  2. Run python app.py.
  3. Add test data via POST (use Postman/curl):
    Bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/episode -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"title": "Test Episode", "file_path": "episode1.mp3"}'
  4. Test browsing: Open http://localhost:5000/episodes in browser.
  5. Test stream: Use HTML5 audio in front-end, or curl with range: curl -r 0-1023 http://localhost:5000/stream/1 > partial.mp3.

This keeps media server-side (streamed in chunks). If you need expansions like user auth, search, or handling large files, reply with details!

You're getting a 404 when trying to browse http://localhost:5000 (or similar). Let's fix it quickly.

Quick checklist – what usually causes this

  1. Is the server actually running?
    • You need to run python app.py (or whatever your file is called) in the terminal.
    • Look for output like:
      text
      * Running on http://127.0.0.1:5000 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
    • If you don't see this → server isn't started → 404 is expected.
  2. Did you visit the correct URL?
    • Default Flask URL is: http://localhost:5000 or http://127.0.0.1:5000
    • But the code I gave has no root route (/), so visiting just localhost:5000/ will give 404.
    • Try these instead:
      • http://localhost:5000/episodes → should return JSON with episodes list
      • http://localhost:5000/episode/1 → if you have an episode with ID 1
  3. Do you have any episodes in the database?
    • If the DB is empty, /episodes will return {"episodes": [], "total": 0, ...}
    • Add at least one episode first (see below).

Step-by-step fix

  1. Make sure server is running:
    Bash
    python app.py
    (or python3 app.py on some systems)
  2. Add a test episode using curl (or Postman):
    Bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/episode \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

should i use http or websoceks

For your podcast website (browse titles + play episodes server-side via HTML5 <audio>), stick with plain HTTP (what you already have with range requests / streaming via send_file).

Why HTTP is the right choice here (clear & concise)

  • Your main job: Serve pre-recorded podcast episodes (on-demand audio files).
  • HTML5 <audio src="/stream/123"> works perfectly with HTTP + Range headers (206 Partial Content).
    • Browser handles seeking, pausing, buffering automatically.
    • No extra code needed on frontend beyond normal <audio controls>.
    • Server just streams chunks → very efficient for large files.
  • This is exactly how almost every podcast / music / video site works for on-demand playback (SoundCloud, Spotify web, YouTube on-demand, etc.).

When WebSockets would actually make sense (not your case)

Use WebSockets (e.g. via Flask-SocketIO) only if you need one or more of these:

  • Real-time live streaming (someone is recording live right now → push new audio chunks as they come).
  • Chat / comments / live reactions synced while listening.
  • Push notifications when new episodes drop (without polling).
  • Very low-latency interactive features (e.g. collaborative listening with sync).

None of that matches "podcast website – prioritize browsing titles and serving media" where media is played server-side.

Quick comparison table for your project

FeatureHTTP (your current setup)WebSockets
Works with <audio> tagYes – native, simpleNo – need custom JS to play buffers
Seeking / pause / resumeBuilt-in by browserYou must implement manually
Setup complexityVery low (you already did it)Medium-high (SocketIO + JS handling)
Overhead per connectionLow for streamingHigher (persistent open conn.)
Scales for many listenersExcellent (CDN-friendly later)Harder (stateful connections)
Best for podcasts?Yes – standard wayNo – overkill

Recommendation

Keep using your current /stream/<id> endpoint with HTTP range support.

Only switch/add WebSockets later if the frontend team asks for real-time features (live shows, chat during episodes, etc.).

If you want to make it even more robust later:

  • Add Accept-Ranges: bytes header explicitly (Flask usually does it).
  • Consider Flask-Compress for gzip if needed.
  • For production → serve static media via nginx/Apache instead of Flask (better performance).

But for school project + concurrent work → HTTP is simpler, faster to implement, and correct for 99% of podcast use cases.

Any specific feature you're thinking might need WebSockets? Or happy to stay HTTP?

is post the correct call or should i use get instead?

Short answer: POST is the correct HTTP method for adding a new episode (what your /episode endpoint does). GET would be wrong here.

Quick rule of thumb (REST style)

  • GET → read / fetch data (safe, no changes, can be repeated, cached, bookmarkable) Examples: list episodes, get one episode details → Use GET for /episodes and /episode/<id>
  • POST → create new resource / submit data that changes the server state Examples: add new episode, upload file, create user account → Use POST for /episode (creating a new episode)

Why not GET for adding?

If you used GET for adding (e.g. GET /episode?title=New&file_path=abc.mp3), these bad things happen:

  • Browser prefetching / crawling could accidentally create episodes
  • People can bookmark / share the link and it would create duplicates
  • Very easy to create episodes by mistake (just refresh page)
  • Not secure — title & path visible in URL / logs
  • Against every REST / HTTP best practice

Your current setup is correct

text
GET    /episodes             → list all (or paginated)
GET    /episode/5            → get details of episode #5
POST   /episode              → create new episode (send JSON body)
GET    /stream/5             → stream/play episode #5

That's standard and exactly what front-end developers expect.

Summary table for your API

ActionMethodEndpointBody?Correct?
List all episodesGET/episodesNoYes
Get one episode detailsGET/episode/<id>NoYes
Add new episodePOST/episodeYes (JSON)Yes
Play/stream episodeGET/stream/<id>NoYes

So: keep POST for adding episodes — don't change it to GET.

If your front-end team is asking why it's POST instead of GET, just show them this explanation (or the table).

Here’s a minimal but functional set of API endpoints for a basic podcast website. I've divided them clearly between Content Creator (people who upload/manage podcasts) and Consumer (listeners who browse and play).

This assumes a simple podcast site: episodes have title, description, audio file, maybe publish date + optional cover image. Streaming is server-side (via range requests, as we already have).

Summary / Outline

  • Consumer (public / listener-facing): Mostly GET calls for browsing + one streaming endpoint.
  • Content Creator (logged-in podcasters): POST/PUT/DELETE for managing content + auth needed.
  • Total: ~8–10 core endpoints to make the site actually work.

If your project is very basic (school level), you can start with just the bold ones.

Consumer / Listener APIs (Frontend for visitors)

These are public or semi-public (no login required for listening).

MethodEndpointPurposeRequired for Functionality?Response Example
GET/episodesList all episodes (titles, descriptions, dates) – main browse pageYes (core)JSON array or paginated list
GET/episodes?search=keyword&page=2&limit=10Search / filter / paginate episodesNice-to-haveSame as above
GET/episode/<id>Get full details of one episode (title, desc, cover, metadata)Yes (episode page)Single episode JSON
GET/stream/<id>Stream the audio file (supports Range headers for seeking)Yes (core – playback)Audio stream (206 Partial Content)
GET/categories or /genresList available categories/genres (if you have them)OptionalArray of strings/categories
GET/recent or /featuredQuick list of newest / popular episodesOptional (homepage)Short list

Minimal consumer set to make site functional:

  • GET /episodes
  • GET /episode/:id
  • GET /stream/:id

→ With these three, visitors can browse titles and actually play episodes via HTML5 <audio>.

Content Creator APIs (Frontend for podcasters / admins)

These require authentication (e.g. JWT, session, or API key). Assume login endpoint exists or use simple token-based auth.

MethodEndpointPurposeRequired?Body (if any)
POST/episodeCreate / upload new episodeYes (core){title, description, file_path, …}
PUT/episode/<id>Update episode (title, desc, etc.)Yes (editing)Partial or full episode object
DELETE/episode/<id>Delete episode (and optionally file)Yes (management)—
POST/upload-audioUpload audio file → returns file_path or temp URLVery usefulMultipart/form-data (file)
GET/my-episodesList only episodes created by current userNice-to-haveList like /episodes but filtered
GET/episode/<id>Same as consumer, but maybe with extra statsOptional—

Minimal creator set to make it functional:

  • POST /episode
  • PUT /episode/:id
  • DELETE /episode/:id
  • (Bonus: POST /upload-audio if you want real file uploads instead of just file_path string)

Recommended Starting Set (Minimal Viable Podcast Site)

Consumer (public):

  1. GET /episodes
  2. GET /episode/<id>
  3. GET /stream/<id>

Creator (authenticated): 4. POST /episode 5. PUT /episode/<id> 6. DELETE /episode/<id>

→ With just these 6 calls, front-end can build:

  • Homepage/list → browse titles
  • Episode detail page → show info + play button
  • Creator dashboard → add/edit/delete own episodes

Everything else (search, categories, upload endpoint, user profiles, favorites, comments…) can be added later.

post creates a json index, how do i upload the actual file?

Great question! Your current /episode POST endpoint creates the metadata (title, description, file_path) in the JSON index (database), but it doesn't actually upload the audio file.

To handle real file uploads (so creators can send the MP3/WAV/etc. directly), you need a separate endpoint for uploading the audio file. This is the standard way:

  1. Upload file first → get back a safe filename or path.
  2. Then send the metadata POST with that path.

Recommended Approach: Two-Step Upload

Step 1: New Endpoint for File Upload

Add this endpoint to your app.py (before if __name__ == '__main__':):

Python
from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename
import uuid
import os

# Ensure upload folder exists
UPLOAD_FOLDER = './media'
os.makedirs(UPLOAD_FOLDER, exist_ok=True)
app.config['UPLOAD_FOLDER'] = UPLOAD_FOLDER

ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS = {'mp3', 'wav', 'm4a', 'ogg'}

def allowed_file(filename):
    return '.' in filename and filename.rsplit('.', 1)[1].lower() in ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS

@app.route('/upload-audio', methods=['POST'])
def upload_audio():
    """
    Upload audio file.
    Returns: JSON with { "file_url": "/stream/<id>", "file_path": "generated_filename.mp3" }
    """
    if 'file' not in request.files:
        return jsonify({"error": "No file part"}), 400
    
    file = request.files['file']
    if file.filename == '':
        return jsonify({"error": "No selected file"}), 400
    
    if file and allowed_file(file.filename):
        # Generate unique filename to avoid overwrites
        ext = file.filename.rsplit('.', 1)[1].lower()
        filename = f"{uuid.uuid4()}.{ext}"
        file_path = os.path.join(app.config['UPLOAD_FOLDER'], filename)
        file.save(file_path)
        
        # Return the relative path (used later in metadata)
        return jsonify({
            "file_path": filename,  # e.g. "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000.mp3"
            "file_url": f"/stream/{filename}"  # Optional hint for frontend
        }), 201
    
    return jsonify({"error": "Invalid file type"}), 400

Step 2: Use It in the Metadata POST

Update your existing /episode POST handler slightly so it accepts the file_path returned from upload:

Python
@app.route('/episode', methods=['POST'])
def add_episode():
    data = request.json
    if not data or not data.get('title') or not data.get('file_path'):
        abort(400, description="Missing title or file_path")
    
    # Optional: Check if file actually exists on server
    full_path = os.path.join(app.config['UPLOAD_FOLDER'], data['file_path'])
    if not os.path.exists(full_path):
        abort(400, description="File path does not exist")
    
    episode = Episode(
        title=data['title'],
        description=data.get('description', ''),
        file_path=data['file_path']  # Store just the filename
    )
    db.session.add(episode)
    db.session.commit()
    return jsonify(episode.to_dict()), 201

How Creators Use It (Workflow)

  1. Upload the file (multipart/form-data)
    Bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/upload-audio \
  -F "file=@/path/to/your/podcast.mp3"
    Response:
    JSON
    {
  "file_path": "a1b2c3d4-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab.mp3",
  "file_url": "/stream/a1b2c3d4-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab.mp3"
}
  2. Create episode metadata using that file_path
    Bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/episode \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "title": "My Awesome Episode",
    "description": "This is great!",
    "file_path": "a1b2c3d4-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab.mp3"
  }'

Bonus: Update Streaming Endpoint to Use Filename

Your current /stream/<int:episode_id> looks up file_path from DB. But if you want to test streaming directly after upload (before metadata), you can add a temporary route:

Python
@app.route('/stream-file/<filename>')
def stream_file(filename):
    file_path = os.path.join(app.config['UPLOAD_FOLDER'], filename)
    if not os.path.exists(file_path):
        abort(404)
    return send_file(file_path, mimetype='audio/mpeg', conditional=True, as_attachment=False)

Why Separate Endpoints?

  • Security: Uploads can be validated separately.
  • Flexibility: Front-end can show progress bar for large files.
  • Simpler: Metadata is JSON, files are binary (multipart).

Quick Summary

  • Add /upload-audio for actual file upload.
  • Use returned file_path in the /episode POST.
  • Keep /stream/<id> for playback (looks up file from DB).

curl: option -F: is badly used here

The error "curl: option -F: is badly used here" usually means there's a syntax mistake in how you're using the -F (or --form) option. Curl is very picky about the format.

Common causes & fixes (most likely yours first)

  1. No space between -F and the argument Wrong:
    Bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/upload-audio -F"file=@episode.mp3"
    Right (add space after -F):
    Bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/upload-audio -F "file=@episode.mp3"
  2. Missing or wrong @ before the file path Wrong:
    Bash
    curl ... -F "file=episode.mp3"          # treats as text field, not file
    Right:
    Bash
    curl ... -F "file=@episode.mp3"         # @ tells curl: "this is a file"
  3. File doesn't exist or path is wrong Curl sometimes complains about -F format if it can't open the file at all. → Double-check:
    Bash
    ls episode.mp3          # or whatever your filename is
    Use full/absolute path if needed:
    Bash
    curl ... -F "file=@/full/path/to/episode.mp3"
  4. Typo or extra characters in the field name Wrong examples that trigger "badly used":
    • -Ffile=@... (no quotes + no =)
    • -F "file : @file.mp3" (extra spaces/colons)
    • -F "file=@file.mp3;type=<something invalid>" (if you added type= with bad value)

Bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/upload-audio \
  -F "file=@my-podcast.mp3"

    curl -v -X POST http://localhost:5000/upload-audio -F "file=@my-podcast.mp3"

C:\Users...\app>curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/upload-audio -F "file=@C:\Pink_Floyd_Time.mp3 "

<!doctype html> <html lang=en> <title>404 Not Found</title> <h1>Not Found</h1> <p>The requested URL was not found on the server. If you entered the URL manually please check your spelling and try again.</p>

The 404 Not Found means your Flask server did not receive the request at all — or more precisely: the /upload-audio route does not exist in the currently running app.

Most likely reasons (in order of probability)

  1. You never added the /upload-audio endpoint code to app.py → You probably only have the original code (with /episode, /stream/<id>, etc.) → Flask returns 404 for any route that isn't explicitly defined
  2. You added the code but didn't restart the server Flask in debug mode usually auto-reloads on file save, but sometimes it fails → especially if you have syntax errors
  3. You are running a different/old version of the file (common when people have app.py, main.py, server.py etc. in the same folder)

Quick fix steps

  1. Verify the code is actually in your file Open app.py (or whatever file you run) and make sure these lines exist near the top/middle:

    Python
    from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename
import uuid
import os

# Folder setup (add near the top, after app = Flask(...))
UPLOAD_FOLDER = './media'
os.makedirs(UPLOAD_FOLDER, exist_ok=True)
app.config['UPLOAD_FOLDER'] = UPLOAD_FOLDER

ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS = {'mp3', 'wav', 'm4a', 'ogg'}

def allowed_file(filename):
    return '.' in filename and \
           filename.rsplit('.', 1)[1].lower() in ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS

# The actual route (add this before if __name__ == '__main__':)
@app.route('/upload-audio', methods=['POST'])
def upload_audio():
    if 'file' not in request.files:
        return jsonify({"error": "No file part"}), 400
    file = request.files['file']
    if file.filename == '':
        return jsonify({"error": "No selected file"}), 400
    if file and allowed_file(file.filename):
        ext = file.filename.rsplit('.', 1)[1].lower()
        filename = f"{uuid.uuid4()}.{ext}"
        file_path = os.path.join(app.config['UPLOAD_FOLDER'], filename)
        file.save(file_path)
        return jsonify({
            "file_path": filename,
            "file_url": f"/stream-file/{filename}"  # or later use episode id
        }), 201
    return jsonify({"error": "File type not allowed"}), 400

  2. Save the file

  3. Stop the server (Ctrl+C in terminal)

  4. Restart it

    Bash
    python app.py

    → Watch for any ImportError or SyntaxError in the terminal — fix those first if they appear.

  5. Test again (use forward slashes even on Windows — curl understands them)

    Bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/upload-audio ^
  -F "file=@C:/Pink_Floyd_Time.mp3"

    Or (alternative syntax — sometimes more reliable on Windows cmd):

    Bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/upload-audio -F file=@C:\Pink_Floyd_Time.mp3

# Podcast Website API Specification

**Base URL**  
`http://localhost:5000`

**Current version**  
v1 (no prefix yet – add `/api/v1` later if needed)

**Content-Type**  
All JSON responses: `application/json`  
POST requests with data: `application/json` (except file uploads)

**Authentication**  
None implemented yet (public endpoints).  
Future: Add JWT or session-based auth for creator endpoints.

## Endpoints Overview

| Method | Endpoint                  | Description                          | Auth required? | Main consumer | Main creator |
|--------|---------------------------|--------------------------------------|----------------|---------------|--------------|
| GET    | `/episodes`               | List episodes (paginated)            | No             | ✓             |              |
| GET    | `/episode/{id}`           | Get single episode details           | No             | ✓             |              |
| GET    | `/stream/{id}`            | Stream audio file (HTML5 audio)      | No             | ✓             |              |
| POST   | `/upload-audio`           | Upload audio file → get file_path    | Yes (future)   |               | ✓            |
| POST   | `/episode`                | Create new episode (metadata)        | Yes (future)   |               | ✓            |
| PUT    | `/episode/{id}`           | Update episode metadata              | Yes (future)   |               | ✓            |
| DELETE | `/episode/{id}`           | Delete episode                       | Yes (future)   |               | ✓            |

## Detailed Endpoint Specification

### 1. List Episodes  
**GET** `/episodes`  

**Query parameters** (all optional)  
- `page`     int    default: 1  
- `limit`    int    default: 10, max ~50  

**Response** 200 OK

3. Stream Audio

GET /stream/{id}

Headers

404 if episode or file missing

4. Upload Audio File

POST /upload-audio

Content-Type multipart/form-data

Form field

Here's a short and clear Architecture.md you can drop in your project root. It's kept brief for a school project.

Markdown
# Architecture.md – Podcast Website Backend

## Overview
Simple Flask-based REST API backend for a podcast website.  
Focus:  
- Browse episode list  
- Stream audio server-side (no client download)  
- Allow creators to upload audio + add metadata  

Two main user roles:  
- **Listener** (public): browse + play  
- **Creator** (future auth): upload + manage episodes  

## Tech Stack
- **Language**: Python 3  
- **Framework**: Flask  
- **Database**: SQLite (via Flask-SQLAlchemy)  
- **File storage**: Local folder (`./media/`)  
- **Streaming**: Flask `send_file` with range support (HTTP 206)  
- **File upload**: Multipart form-data (`werkzeug`)  
- **Run locally**: `python app.py` → http://localhost:5000  

## Folder Structure (current)

project/ ├── app.py # Main Flask app + all routes ├── podcasts.db # SQLite database (auto-created) ├── media/ # Audio files (gitignored) │ └── *.mp3 / *.m4a ├── API-spec.md # API documentation for frontend team └── Architecture.md # This file

text
## Core Components

1. **Database** (SQLite)
   - Table: `Episode`
   - Fields: id (PK), title, description, file_path (just filename, e.g. "uuid.mp3")

2. **Key Endpoints / Flow**

Creator workflow: POST /upload-audio → upload file → returns {file_path: "uuid.mp3"} ↓ POST /episode → send {title, description, file_path} → creates DB entry

Listener workflow: GET /episodes → list titles + metadata ↓ GET /episode/{id} → details ↓ GET /stream/{id} → HTML5 <audio> plays file from disk (range requests)

text
3. **Streaming Mechanism**
- Uses `send_file(..., conditional=True, as_attachment=False)`
- Browser sends `Range: bytes=...` → Flask returns partial content (206)
- Supports seek, pause, resume natively in `<audio controls>`

4. **File Handling**
- Uploads saved to `./media/` with UUID filename
- Only filename stored in DB (not full path)
- Allowed extensions: mp3, wav, m4a, ogg

## Current Limitations / Future Improvements
- No authentication yet (anyone can upload)
- No pagination/search on frontend side (API supports ?page & ?limit)
- Local file storage only (production → S3 + CloudFront or nginx alias)
- No episode cover images
- No categories/tags/playlists
- SQLite → switch to PostgreSQL/MySQL for real use

## Deployment Notes
- Development: `flask run --debug`
- Production ideas: Gunicorn + Nginx (serve /media statically)

Last updated: Jan 2026

Recommended DB Change (clear & flexible)

New model: Show (you can rename to Podcast, Series, Program, Creator — whatever fits your naming)

Python
# In your models section (add after Episode class)

class Show(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = db.Column(db.String(200), nullable=False)          # e.g. "The Daily Tech", "Albin's Music Corner"
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=True)
    creator_name = db.Column(db.String(100), nullable=True)   # optional: host name, band name, etc.
    cover_image_path = db.Column(db.String(200), nullable=True)  # optional future
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            'id': self.id,
            'name': self.name,
            'description': self.description,
            'creator_name': self.creator_name
        }

# Update existing Episode model – add relationship
class Episode(db.Model):
    # ... existing fields ...
    show_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('show.id'), nullable=False)
    show = db.relationship('Show', backref=db.backref('episodes', lazy=True))

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            'id': self.id,
            'title': self.title,
            'description': self.description,
            'file_path': self.file_path,
            'show_id': self.show_id,
            'show_name': self.show.name if self.show else None   # nice to have
        }

  3. Restart the app → db.create_all() will recreate tables with the new structure.
    • All old episodes will be lost → if you have test data you care about, export it first or add a quick migration script (ask if needed).

(For real projects you'd use Flask-Migrate / Alembic, but for school that's usually overkill.)

Updated / New Endpoints (add these)

Python
# 1. List all shows
@app.route('/shows', methods=['GET'])
def get_shows():
    shows = Show.query.all()
    return jsonify([s.to_dict() for s in shows])

# 2. Get one show + its episodes (very useful for frontend)
@app.route('/show/<int:show_id>', methods=['GET'])
def get_show(show_id):
    show = Show.query.get_or_404(show_id)
    episodes = Episode.query.filter_by(show_id=show_id).all()
    return jsonify({
        'show': show.to_dict(),
        'episodes': [e.to_dict() for e in episodes]
    })

# 3. Filter episodes by show (add to existing /episodes)
@app.route('/episodes', methods=['GET'])
def get_episodes():
    query = Episode.query
    show_id = request.args.get('show_id', type=int)
    if show_id:
        query = query.filter_by(show_id=show_id)
    
    page = request.args.get('page', 1, type=int)
    limit = request.args.get('limit', 10, type=int)
    pagination = query.paginate(page=page, per_page=limit, error_out=False)
    
    return jsonify({
        'episodes': [ep.to_dict() for ep in pagination.items],
        'total': pagination.total,
        'pages': pagination.pages,
        'current_page': pagination.page
    })

# 4. Create new show (for creators)
@app.route('/show', methods=['POST'])
def add_show():
    data = request.json
    if not data or not data.get('name'):
        abort(400, "Missing name")
    
    show = Show(
        name=data['name'],
        description=data.get('description'),
        creator_name=data.get('creator_name')
    )
    db.session.add(show)
    db.session.commit()
    return jsonify(show.to_dict()), 201

# 5. When creating episode → require show_id
@app.route('/episode', methods=['POST'])
def add_episode():
    data = request.json
    required = ['title', 'file_path', 'show_id']
    if not data or not all(k in data for k in required):
        abort(400, f"Missing one of: {required}")
    
    # Optional: validate show exists
    if not Show.query.get(data['show_id']):
        abort(404, "Show not found")
    
    episode = Episode(
        title=data['title'],
        description=data.get('description'),
        file_path=data['file_path'],
        show_id=data['show_id']
    )
    db.session.add(episode)
    db.session.commit()
    return jsonify(episode.to_dict()), 201

updated endpoints for all previous get /episodes

Here's the updated /episodes endpoint (and related GET endpoints) with the new show/supercategory structure.

Summary / Outline

  • /episodes now supports filtering by show_id
  • Returns show_name in each episode for easier frontend display
  • Keeps pagination (?page=, ?limit=)
  • Added optional sorting (newest first by default)
  • Related: /shows and /show/<id> remain unchanged but complement this

Just replace your current @app.route('/episodes', methods=['GET']) with this updated version.

Python
from datetime import datetime  # if not already imported

@app.route('/episodes', methods=['GET'])
def get_episodes():
    """
    List episodes – now with filtering by show_id
    Query params:
    - show_id     (int)     Filter by specific show/podcast
    - page        (int)     default 1
    - limit       (int)     default 10
    - sort        (str)     'newest' (default), 'oldest', 'title'
    - search      (str)     Optional keyword in title or description
    """
    query = Episode.query

    # Filter by show
    show_id = request.args.get('show_id', type=int)
    if show_id:
        query = query.filter_by(show_id=show_id)

    # Optional search in title or description
    search = request.args.get('search')
    if search:
        search_term = f"%{search}%"
        query = query.filter(
            (Episode.title.ilike(search_term)) |
            (Episode.description.ilike(search_term))
        )

    # Sorting
    sort = request.args.get('sort', 'newest')
    if sort == 'newest':
        query = query.order_by(Episode.id.desc())  # assuming higher ID = newer
        # Alternative if you add publish_date:
        # query = query.order_by(Episode.publish_date.desc())
    elif sort == 'oldest':
        query = query.order_by(Episode.id.asc())
    elif sort == 'title':
        query = query.order_by(Episode.title.asc())

    # Pagination
    page = request.args.get('page', 1, type=int)
    limit = request.args.get('limit', 10, type=int)
    pagination = query.paginate(page=page, per_page=limit, error_out=False)

    episodes = pagination.items

    return jsonify({
        "episodes": [ep.to_dict() for ep in episodes],
        "total": pagination.total,
        "pages": pagination.pages,
        "current_page": pagination.page,
        "per_page": limit,
        "applied_filters": {
            "show_id": show_id if show_id else None,
            "search": search if search else None,
            "sort": sort
        }
    }), 200

Here's a clear, step-by-step way to do it without breaking anything.

Summary / Outline

  4. Minor cleanup in app.py

Step-by-step

1. Create routes.py in the same folder as app.py

Python
# routes.py
from flask import Blueprint, jsonify, request, send_file, abort
import os
from . import db   # relative import – assumes app.py is in same folder
from .models import Episode, Show  # adjust if you have separate models.py

# Create Blueprint
bp = Blueprint('api', __name__, url_prefix='')

# ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Consumer / Listener endpoints
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────

@bp.route('/episodes', methods=['GET'])
def get_episodes():
    query = Episode.query

    show_id = request.args.get('show_id', type=int)
    if show_id:
        query = query.filter_by(show_id=show_id)

    search = request.args.get('search')
    if search:
        search_term = f"%{search}%"
        query = query.filter(
            (Episode.title.ilike(search_term)) |
            (Episode.description.ilike(search_term))
        )

    sort = request.args.get('sort', 'newest')
    if sort == 'newest':
        query = query.order_by(Episode.id.desc())
    elif sort == 'oldest':
        query = query.order_by(Episode.id.asc())
    elif sort == 'title':
        query = query.order_by(Episode.title.asc())

    page = request.args.get('page', 1, type=int)
    limit = request.args.get('limit', 10, type=int)
    pagination = query.paginate(page=page, per_page=limit, error_out=False)

    return jsonify({
        "episodes": [ep.to_dict() for ep in pagination.items],
        "total": pagination.total,
        "pages": pagination.pages,
        "current_page": pagination.page,
        "per_page": limit,
        "applied_filters": {
            "show_id": show_id if show_id else None,
            "search": search if search else None,
            "sort": sort
        }
    }), 200


@bp.route('/episode/<int:episode_id>', methods=['GET'])
def get_episode(episode_id):
    episode = Episode.query.get_or_404(episode_id)
    return jsonify(episode.to_dict())


@bp.route('/stream/<int:episode_id>', methods=['GET'])
def stream_episode(episode_id):
    episode = Episode.query.get_or_404(episode_id)
    file_path = os.path.join(current_app.config['MEDIA_FOLDER'], episode.file_path)
    
    if not os.path.exists(file_path):
        abort(404, description="Media file not found")
    
    return send_file(
        file_path,
        mimetype='audio/mpeg',
        conditional=True,
        as_attachment=False
    )


@bp.route('/shows', methods=['GET'])
def get_shows():
    shows = Show.query.all()
    return jsonify([s.to_dict() for s in shows])


@bp.route('/show/<int:show_id>', methods=['GET'])
def get_show(show_id):
    show = Show.query.get_or_404(show_id)
    episodes = Episode.query.filter_by(show_id=show_id).all()
    return jsonify({
        'show': show.to_dict(),
        'episodes': [e.to_dict() for e in episodes]
    })

current_app.config['MEDIA_FOLDER']

where is this defined?

current_app.config['MEDIA_FOLDER'] is defined in your main application file — most likely app.py (the one where you create the Flask app instance).

Where exactly it's set

Look for these lines (usually near the top, right after app = Flask(__name__)):

Python
# app.py (or main file)

app = Flask(__name__)

# ... other imports and config ...

app.config['MEDIA_FOLDER'] = './media'          # ← this line defines it

# or sometimes written as:
app.config['MEDIA_FOLDER'] = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'media')

os.makedirs(app.config['MEDIA_FOLDER'], exist_ok=True)  # optional but good

Why current_app instead of app?

In routes.py (which is a separate module), you cannot directly import app from app.py without creating a circular import problem.

So Flask provides current_app — a proxy that always points to the currently running Flask application instance.

You need to import it in routes.py:

Python
# routes.py – add this at the top if not already there
from flask import current_app

Then you can safely use:

Python
file_path = os.path.join(current_app.config['MEDIA_FOLDER'], episode.file_path)

Quick checklist – make sure it's all there

In app.py:

  • app.config['MEDIA_FOLDER'] = './media' (or similar path)
  • os.makedirs(app.config['MEDIA_FOLDER'], exist_ok=True) (optional but prevents errors)

In routes.py (or wherever you use it):

  • from flask import current_app

If you still get KeyError: 'MEDIA_FOLDER' → the key was never set → check app.py for typos or missing line.

# Folder setup (add near the top, after app = Flask(...)) UPLOAD_FOLDER = './media' os.makedirs(UPLOAD_FOLDER, exist_ok=True) app.config['UPLOAD_FOLDER'] = UPLOAD_FOLDER ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS = {'mp3', 'wav', 'm4a', 'ogg'} def allowed_file(filename): return '.' in filename and \ filename.rsplit('.', 1)[1].lower() in ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS

should this be placed in routes.py or app.py?

Short answer: Put it in app.py (the main file where app = Flask(__name__) is created).

Why app.py and not routes.py?

  • app.config belongs to the application instance (app).
  • Configuration values (like UPLOAD_FOLDER, ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS) are global app settings → they should live where the app is created and configured.
  • routes.py is only for route handlers and business logic — it should not contain app-level configuration or folder creation code.

Correct placement (in app.py)

Python
# app.py

from flask import Flask
import os
from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

app = Flask(__name__)

# ── Config ───────────────────────────────────────────────
app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///podcasts.db'
app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False

# Media / upload config  ← put it here
UPLOAD_FOLDER = './media'
os.makedirs(UPLOAD_FOLDER, exist_ok=True)
app.config['UPLOAD_FOLDER'] = UPLOAD_FOLDER

ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS = {'mp3', 'wav', 'm4a', 'ogg'}

# You can also put the helper function here (it's fine)
def allowed_file(filename):
    return '.' in filename and \
           filename.rsplit('.', 1)[1].lower() in ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS

# If you want to use allowed_file in routes.py, export it:
# (add this at the bottom of app.py)
__all__ = ['allowed_file']   # optional but clean

db = SQLAlchemy(app)

# Register blueprint
from routes import bp
app.register_blueprint(bp)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    with app.app_context():
        db.create_all()
    app.run(debug=True)

How routes.py uses it

In routes.py you only read the config (never write to it):

Python
# routes.py
from flask import current_app, request, jsonify, abort

# Use it like this:
@app.route('/upload-audio', methods=['POST'])
def upload_audio():
    if 'file' not in request.files:
        return jsonify({"error": "No file part"}), 400
    
    file = request.files['file']
    if file.filename == '' or not allowed_file(file.filename):
        return jsonify({"error": "Invalid or no file"}), 400
    
    # Access config safely
    upload_folder = current_app.config['UPLOAD_FOLDER']
    
    # ... rest of your upload logic ...

Summary – placement rule of thumb

ThingPut inReason
app = Flask(...)app.pyCore app creation
app.config[...] settingsapp.pyGlobal config
os.makedirs(...) for foldersapp.pyDone once at startup
ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS setapp.pyApp-wide constant
def allowed_file(...)app.py (or utils.py)Reusable helper
@bp.route(...) functionsroutes.pyRoute logic only

So: app.py gets the config block, routes.py only imports and uses current_app.config when needed.

    # models.py
from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy
from datetime import datetime

db = SQLAlchemy()

class Show(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = db.Column(db.String(200), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=True)
    creator_name = db.Column(db.String(100), nullable=True)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            'id': self.id,
            'name': self.name,
            'description': self.description,
            'creator_name': self.creator_name
        }

class Episode(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(200), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=True)
    file_path = db.Column(db.String(200), nullable=False)
    show_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('show.id'), nullable=False)
    show = db.relationship('Show', backref='episodes', lazy=True)

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            'id': self.id,
            'title': self.title,
            'description': self.description,
            'file_path': self.file_path,
            'show_id': self.show_id,
            'show_name': self.show.name if self.show else None
        }

db = SQLAlchemy(app) is missing

Yes, that's the issue.

In your current setup (with models in models.py), you must not do db = SQLAlchemy(app) in app.py anymore.

Instead:

Python
# app.py

from flask import Flask
import os
from models import db   # ← import the shared db instance

app = Flask(__name__)

app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///podcasts.db'
app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False
app.config['MEDIA_FOLDER'] = './media'
os.makedirs(app.config['MEDIA_FOLDER'], exist_ok=True)

# Initialize the db with the app (VERY IMPORTANT)
db.init_app(app)

# Register blueprint
from routes import bp
app.register_blueprint(bp)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    with app.app_context():
        db.create_all()          # creates tables if they don't exist
    app.run(debug=True)

Why this way?

  • db = SQLAlchemy() lives in models.py (no app yet)
  • db.init_app(app) connects it to your Flask app
  • This avoids circular imports and keeps models clean/reusable

After this change:

  • Restart the server
  • The .models cannot be resolved should disappear
  • Tables should be created on first run

add episode to default 'show' if omitted

To make show_id optional in POST /episode and default to a specific "fallback" show (e.g. ID=1 or name="Default Show"):

1. Ensure a default show exists

Run this once (e.g. in a setup script or manually via curl/REPL):

# One-time creation (add to app.py or run separately)
with app.app_context():
    if not Show.query.filter_by(name="Default Podcast").first():
        default_show = Show(name="Default Podcast", description="Fallback show for uncategorized episodes")

2. Update add_episode() in routes.py

Python
@bp.route('/episode', methods=['POST'])
def add_episode():
    data = request.json
    if not data or not data.get('title') or not data.get('file_path'):
        abort(400, description="Missing title or file_path")

    # Default logic
    show_id = data.get('show_id')
    if show_id is None:
        default_show = Show.query.filter_by(name="Default Podcast").first()
        if not default_show:
            abort(500, description="Default show not found – create it first")
        show_id = default_show.id

    # Validate chosen/default show exists
    show = Show.query.get(show_id)
    if not show:
        abort(404, description="Show not found")

    episode = Episode(
        title=data['title'],
        description=data.get('description', ''),
        file_path=data['file_path'],
        show_id=show_id
    )
    db.session.add(episode)
    db.session.commit()

    return jsonify(episode.to_dict()), 201

Alternative: Hardcode default ID=1 (simpler, less safe)

show_id = data.get('show_id', 1)  # defaults to show #1
    show = Show.query.get(show_id)
    if not show:
        abort(404, description=f"Show {show_id} not found")

Recommendation

Use the name-based lookup version ("Default Podcast") — it's more readable and survives ID changes.

i move 'allowed_file' to utils.py and now im getting some serious sqlalchemy errors. way too much to paste here. i just moved and then wrote *from utils.py import allowed_name

The error is almost certainly a circular import caused by moving allowed_file to utils.py while one or more files still try to import from each other in a loop.

Common pattern that breaks after this change:

Python
# routes.py          → imports utils
# utils.py           → imports models (or db)
# models.py          → imports app / db.init_app (sometimes)
# app.py             → imports routes

→ loop → SQLAlchemy fails during initialization (very common symptom).

Quick fixes (try in this order – start with #1)

  1. Remove any import from utils.py back to app/models/routes Open utils.py and make sure it has zero imports from your own modules. It should look like this (minimal & safe):

    Python
    # utils.py   ← no imports from app, models, routes etc.

ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS = {'mp3', 'wav', 'm4a', 'ogg'}

def allowed_file(filename):
    return '.' in filename and \
           filename.rsplit('.', 1)[1].lower() in ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS

  2. Fix the import line you wrote You wrote *from utils.py import allowed_name — that's wrong syntax and wrong name.

    Correct versions (choose one):

    Python
    # Option A – most common
from utils import allowed_file

# Option B – if utils.py is in same folder
from .utils import allowed_file

# Option C – absolute (safest when confused)
from utils import allowed_file

    Do not use * (wildcard) here — it hides what you're actually importing.

  3. Restart everything

    • Close terminal
    • Delete podcasts.db if you're okay losing test data (forces clean recreate)
    • Run python app.py again

  4. If still broken – minimal test Temporarily comment out all route decorators in routes.py except one simple GET (e.g. /shows). If the server starts → problem is inside one of the route functions → slowly uncomment them one by one.

If you want fastest path forward right now

Move allowed_file back into app.py (or routes.py where it's used) for 5 minutes. Get the app running again, then we can refactor utils properly without breaking SQLAlchemy.

The error is clear:

text

Could not determine join condition between parent/child tables on relationship Episode.Collection

Root cause You have (or had) a relationship defined in the Episode model that points to a class named Collection, but:

  • there is noCollection model defined anymore, or
  • the foreign key column in Episode still references 'collection.id' instead of 'show.id', or
  • you renamed Show → Collection (or vice versa) but didn't update the relationship / foreign key properly.

SQLAlchemy is trying to configure a relationship Episode.collection (or similar) that no longer matches the actual tables/columns.

Quick fix steps

  1. Delete podcasts.db (safest way to force clean start – you lose test data but avoid migration hell)

    Bash

    or just rename it to podcasts-old.db

    Python
    # models.py – make sure it looks EXACTLY like this (no Collection!)

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy
from datetime import datetime

db = SQLAlchemy()

class Show(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'show'          # optional but clearer
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = db.Column(db.String(200), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=True)
    creator_name = db.Column(db.String(100), nullable=True)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

    def to_dict(self):
        return { ... }  # your dict

class Episode(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'episode'
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(200), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=True)
    file_path = db.Column(db.String(200), nullable=False)
    
    show_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('show.id'), nullable=False)   # ← must point to 'show.id'
    
    show = db.relationship('Show', backref='episodes', lazy=True)               # ← must be 'Show'

    def to_dict(self):
        return { ... }

    Important: Search your models.py / routes.py / app.py for the word Collection – delete any line that mentions Collection, collection, or Episode.collection.

  3. Restart the app

    py app\app.py

You wrote 'Collection.id' (capital C) in the ForeignKey string.

Fix – two clean options (pick one)

Option 1 – Recommended (clean & future-proof)

Python
class Episode(db.Model):

    collection = db.relationship('Collection', backref='episodes', lazy=True)             # ← lowercase 'collection' is fine as attribute name

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            'id': self.id,
            'title': self.title,
            'description': self.description,
            'file_path': self.file_path,
            'collection_id': self.collection_id,
            'collection_name': self.collection.name if self.collection else None
        }

    Collection = db.relationship('Collection', backref='episodes', lazy=True)

Yes, I understand — the foreign key error appeared suddenly after moving allowed_file to utils.py.

Why did this happen now?

Even though you didn't touch the models, Python module loading order changed slightly after the move + new import.

Before:

  • app.py → imports routes.py → routes imports models/db → everything loads in a certain sequence

After moving allowed_file:

  • New import chain / timing → SQLAlchemy tries to configure relationships before all classes are fully defined
  • This makes the "missing table" error surface even though the code was technically always wrong (just hidden by lucky loading order)

It's a classic latent circular-import / configuration timing bug in SQLAlchemy — very common when refactoring imports.

What to do now (fastest recovery)

  1. Use this exact Episode model block (copy-paste replace the old one):

    file_path = db.Column(db.String(200), nullable=False)

    collection = db.relationship('Collection', backref='episodes', lazy=True)

            'id': self.id,
            'title': self.title,
            'description': self.description,
            'file_path': self.file_path,
            'collection_id': self.collection_id,

        }

You're right — it did work before, even with the code being technically incorrect. That's frustrating, but here's the short explanation why it suddenly broke after moving allowed_file:

Python loads files top to bottom and left to right. The order in which classes are seen matters when one refers to another by name.

Before the move:

  • The import order / timing was lucky — Collection got defined before SQLAlchemy tried to inspect Episode.collection_id
  • SQLAlchemy didn't complain during startup (even though the ForeignKey string was wrong)

After moving allowed_file to utils.py:

  • You added a new import
  • This changed the exact sequence Python loads modules
  • Now SQLAlchemy inspects relationships earlier (before Collection class is fully read)
  • → NameError or table-not-found error appears

It's not that the code "broke" — it was always fragile, and the refactor just made the fragility visible.

Quickest way to make it work again (right now)

Replace your current Episode class with this:

Python
class Episode(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(200), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=True)
    file_path = db.Column(db.String(200), nullable=False)

    # Use string for ForeignKey → no NameError even if Collection is defined later
    collection_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('collection.id'), nullable=False)
    
    # Relationship can stay with class name (SQLAlchemy resolves it later)
    collection = db.relationship('Collection', backref='episodes', lazy=True)

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            'id': self.id,
            'title': self.title,
            'description': self.description,
            'file_path': self.file_path,
            'collection_id': self.collection_id,
            'collection_name': self.collection.name if self.collection else None
        }

  3. Run the app again

Bash

After the change → restart the server and try again.

and to stream it

To stream the uploaded episode (e.g. the one with file_path cbefcd9a-c475-41dc-81a7-d819d4058897.wav)

Use this endpoint:

text
GET http://localhost:5000/stream/{episode_id}

Steps to stream it

  1. Find the episode id After you successfully created the episode, you got back something like this in the response:

    JSON
    {
  "id": 3,
  "title": "Test Episode 1",
  "description": "My test wav file",
  "file_path": "cbefcd9a-c475-41dc-81a7-d819d4058897.wav",
  "collection_id": 1,
  "collection_name": "tt"
}

    Note the value of "id" (in this example: 3)

  2. Stream URL Use the episode id in the URL:

    text
    http://localhost:5000/stream/3

  3. Quick test options

    • Browser: Paste the URL directly → browser should start playing the audio
    • Simple HTML test page (create a file test.html):
      HTML
      <!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<body>
  <h2>Test Streaming</h2>
  <audio controls>
    <source src="http://localhost:5000/stream/3" type="audio/wav">
    Your browser does not support the audio element.
  </audio>
</body>
</html>
    • Command line (partial download test):
      Bash
      curl -I http://localhost:5000/stream/3
      You should see 206 Partial Content support and Content-Type: audio/wav

Let me know the episode id you got from the POST response, and I'll give you the exact streaming URL. Or if you get any error when trying to stream — paste the error message or status code.
